classification.difficultyReason: Introduce parallel lines at successive bends and link transferred sectors to obtain the final angle.

spec.description: Open zigzag with four bends, matching down-right parallel markers on its two end arms, a right-angle square at the first valley, 110 degrees at the first peak, 115 degrees at the next valley and alpha at the final peak. No printed vertex names.
spec.mathematics: End arms are parallel. Coordinates enforce the stated 90, 110 and 115 degree constraints and give alpha = 95 degrees; segment lengths are drawing parameters, not givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, parallel markers, right-angle square and alpha are visible.

answer.worked:
Construct dashed lines through the $110^\circ$ and $115^\circ$ bends, parallel to the marked end arms. Let the new angles be $u$ and $v$, as shown.

The first connector makes $90^\circ$ with the constructed parallel (corresponding angles on parallel lines).
$$\begin{align*}90^\circ+u&=110^\circ\\u&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
The same connector makes $u$ with the parallel at the next bend (alternate angles on parallel lines).
$$\begin{align*}20^\circ+v&=115^\circ\\v&=95^\circ\\\alpha&=95^\circ\end{align*}$$
The last equality uses alternate angles on parallel lines.

spec.description: Complete question figure with dashed red auxiliary parallels through the two middle bends. u labels the portion of the 110-degree angle beside the descending connector; v labels the portion of the 115-degree angle beside the rising connector.
spec.mathematics: u = 20 degrees, v = 95 degrees and alpha = v. The constructed directions are parallel to both marked end arms.
